item.title: Rust Has No GC — Concurrency Still Breaks: 100 Threads Fighting Over One Counter Lose 51%~81% of Updates (Measured)
item.description: “No GC, therefore safe concurrency” is a misconception. Rust pushes data races to compile time and leaves deadlocks and logic bugs at runtime. 100 threads × 100k increments on one shared counter: 51%~81% of updates lost in 5 rounds on -O0; 0 lost under -O — under UB, correctness is luck. All examples reproducible: double-lock deadlock, RefCell/Mutex/Atomic postures, Rc vs Arc.

item.title: Rust Concurrency Explained: A Guide to Arc, Mutex, and Channels for Thread Safety
item.description: Deep dive into Rust's core concurrency concepts: Arc atomic reference counting, Mutex mutual exclusion, and Channel communication. Learn thread-safe concurrent programming through vivid analogies and practical code examples.
